title: Season 1, Ep 4: Never connect apps directly to an LLM
oneliner: Put an AI gateway between your enterprise applications and the LLM providers - it load-balances, throttles, rate-limits, and tracks every token.
says: If you plan to connect an enterprise application to an LLM, do not connect directly - it creates many problems. Use an AI gateway between your applications and the LLM service providers: it load-balances across multiple LLM providers, provides automated throttling and rate limiting, and helps you monitor and trace your tokens across providers.
explained: The direct-connection anti-pattern is how most first AI features are built - an API key in the app, one provider, no controls. It works in a demo and breaks in production: no failover when the provider degrades, no protection when a bug loops requests into a five-figure token bill, no visibility into who is spending what.

The gateway converts all of that into platform behavior. Load balancing across providers gives resilience and negotiating leverage. Throttling and rate limiting turn cost spikes into queued work. Token monitoring and tracing is the inference economy made observable - you cannot optimize spend you cannot see. This pattern reappears at platform scale in Season 2: the gateway is the infrastructure half, and the prompt registry, evaluation platform, and tool catalog are the governance half of the same front door.
takeaway: An AI gateway is non-negotiable infrastructure: resilience across providers, cost controls, and token observability in one layer.
